headline: Revenue and profit climb as guidance moves higher
summary_short: Revenue rose 18.2% y/y to $1.55 billion and net income attributable to TKO grew 3.3% to $101.6 million as Adjusted EBITDA (company-defined, non-GAAP) climbed 23% to $649.9 million; the company raised full-year revenue and Adjusted EBITDA guidance.
summary_long: Growth was broad-based: UFC revenue +29% on new Paramount media rights and UFC Freedom 250, WWE +12% on the new ESPN deal, and IMG +16% on FIFA World Cup 2026 hospitality at On Location. Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 42% from 40%, though net income growth was tempered by legal costs tied to WWE stockholder litigation and higher interest expense on increased debt. TKO raised FY2026 guidance to $5.775-5.825B revenue and $2.275-2.305B Adjusted EBITDA, up from $5.675-5.775B and $2.240-2.290B issued in February. Cash fell q/q to $592.5 million after an $800 million accelerated share repurchase and a $0.79/share dividend; long-term debt rose y/y on new borrowings funding buybacks, with just over $1 billion remaining under authorization.

drivers.explanation: CEO Ariel Emanuel cited "strong momentum heading into the back half of the year"; COO Mark Shapiro said the guidance raise reflects performance to date and confidence in the multi-year trajectory.
Release attributes the increase to UFC (+$119.8M, new Paramount deal, UFC Freedom 250), WWE (+$64.7M, new ESPN deal), and IMG (+$48.1M, FIFA World Cup hospitality at On Location).
Tracks the 3.3% y/y rise in net income attributable to TKO combined with an 8.5% y/y drop in weighted average basic shares from continued buybacks.

Diluted EPS growth outpaces net income's 3.3% rise because the diluted share count fell 61.9% y/y — not from buybacks, but because TKO's two-class Up-C EPS test excluded convertible non-controlling-interest units this quarter as antidilutive.
Revenue growth was partially offset by higher direct operating costs and SG&A, including legal fees and settlement costs tied to WWE stockholder litigation.
Growth trails operating income because net interest expense rose $22.4M y/y to $70.6M, reflecting higher debt balances used to help fund the buyback program.

Total consolidated net income grew 11.3% y/y to $303.9M, but income attributable to TKO grew only 3.3% because non-controlling interests' allocated share rose 15.7% to $202.3M under the Up-C structure.
Cash flow statement shows $967.6M used for share repurchases and $117.3M for dividends in H1 2026, partly offset by $929.9M in new borrowings, consistent with the quarter's cash decline.
Matches $929.9M of new borrowings drawn in H1 2026 per the financing-activities section, used to help fund the ASR and ongoing buyback program.
Current portion of long-term debt scaled with the same H1 2026 borrowings that lifted the long-term debt balance.
Equity attributable to TKO fell y/y as $967.6M of H1 2026 share repurchases outweighed retained-earnings growth from net income.

Reflects the Up-C anti-dilution test excluding convertible non-controlling-interest units this quarter, not a real reduction in shares outstanding; actual buybacks show in basic shares, down 8.5% y/y.
